newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber end mostly up, spot lower with cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber end mostly up, spot lower with cash.

text.p: Reports of continued weakness in cash lumber and rolling out of long positions kept March CME lumber futures pressured at the close while back months posted gains on a better housing outlook, traders said.
Lumber closed $3.60 per tbf lower to $5.50 higher with only March off at $382.00 and May up $2.80 at $383.70.

An unexpectedly large rise in the January new home sales report and technical firmness combined to lift CME lumber futures early. But prices eased back and March fell for a loss on pressure attributed to the continued weak undertone to cash, traders said.

Cash sources anticipated another $5 to $10 decline in the cash spruce price following slow cash trade. Retailer demand was slow and wholesalers appeared to have adequate supplies on hand to meet current demand, they said.
"There's plenty of wood in the pipeline," one cash connected trader said.

Most months were up on expectations of increased housing demand. The U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes during January were up 8.6 percent to an annual rate of 870,000 units, well above expectations. Low interest rates should keep housing strong, they said.
"That's (January report) the best level since March 1986. Obviously, if we are selling homes we are going to be building some," said Curt Cunningham, President of Pacific Futures Trading.
